outline.section: H2: Why Sensitive Skin Reacts to Most Body Lotions
outline.guidance: Explain the mechanics of why conventional lotions irritate sensitive skin. Cover the two main culprits: (1) synthetic fragrance — the single leading cause of contact dermatitis in skincare, cite a credible source such as the American Contact Dermatitis Society or a published dermatology study; (2) preservatives and fillers like parabens, formaldehyde-releasing agents, and artificial dyes. Mention that 'fragrance-free' and 'unscented' are not the same thing — unscented products often contain masking fragrances. Use this section to build reader trust and establish the brand's clean-ingredient philosophy without naming competitors.

outline.section: H2: Ingredients to Look for in a Body Lotion for Sensitive Skin
outline.guidance: Create a clearly structured breakdown of hero ingredients that calm, hydrate, and repair the skin barrier without causing irritation. Cover: (1) Ceramides — explain their role in reinforcing the skin's lipid barrier; cite a peer-reviewed source, e.g., Draelos ZD or a published dermatology journal confirming ceramide efficacy for barrier repair. (2) Coconut oil — note its lauric acid content (approximately 49% of fatty acid composition per published lipid analyses) and documented antimicrobial and emollient properties; include a citation. (3) Aloe vera — soothing, anti-inflammatory properties supported by published research. (4) Shea butter — occlusive moisturizer with anti-inflammatory triterpenes. (5) Oat extract (colloidal oatmeal) — FDA-recognized skin protectant. For each ingredient, keep descriptions concise and benefit-led. Do NOT frame this as a comparison of other brands' formulas.

outline.section: H2: Ingredients to Avoid If You Have Sensitive Skin
outline.guidance: Mirror the previous section with a clear list of ingredients that commonly trigger reactions in sensitive skin. Include: synthetic fragrance (parfum), parabens, SLS/SLES (sulfates), artificial dyes (FD&C colorants), alcohol denat (drying), formaldehyde-releasing preservatives (DMDM hydantoin, quaternium-15). For each, give a one-sentence explanation of why it's problematic for sensitive skin. Keep this educational and empowering — the goal is to teach the reader to read ingredient labels, which naturally reinforces the clean-ingredient positioning of Real Skin Care. Avoid brand-shaming language.

outline.section: H2: How to Apply Body Lotion for Maximum Benefit on Sensitive Skin
outline.guidance: This section is a unique utility play — no top competitor covers application technique in depth. Include: (1) Apply within 3 minutes of showering to lock in moisture while skin is still slightly damp (the 'soak and seal' method, referenced in dermatology guidance for eczema management). (2) Use gentle, upward strokes — avoid rubbing aggressively, which can activate mast cells and trigger redness. (3) Use fragrance-free formulas especially after shaving or exfoliating when the barrier is most vulnerable. (4) Patch-test any new lotion on the inner forearm for 24 hours before full application.
